theme: Product-launch monitors: certificate transparency (crt.sh) tooling, app release-notes scrapers, Wayback diff tools, help-center change monitors, trademark/patent (USPTO, PatentsView) clients
queries_run: gh search repos "crt.sh certificate transparency python" --sort stars
gh search repos "wayback machine diff" --sort stars
gh search repos "uspto trademark api" --sort stars
gh search repos "app store release notes scraper" --sort stars
gh search repos "help center change monitor scraper" --sort stars
gh search repos "certificate transparency subdomain monitor" --sort stars

candidates.name: ropensci/patentsview
candidates.what_it_holds: R client (ropensci-vetted, 39 stars, active as of Jul 2026) to the free PatentsView API (USPTO bulk patent data). No data committed; wraps query/fieldsets/subscore endpoints for patent search, assignees, inventors, CPC classes. Could pull Airbnb's own patent filings (assignee='Airbnb') and counts over time as a product-development-pace proxy.
candidates.why_useful: Addresses gap #15 (patents/trademarks as company-structure/product-launch signal) — patent filing counts/timing can be a lagging proxy for feature roadmap and M&A-adjacent R&D. Free API, no key required in most PatentsView modes.

candidates.name: volfpeter/uspto-patent-citation-graph
candidates.what_it_holds: Python tool (MIT, 16 stars, updated Aug 2026) that downloads patent citation data on-demand from USPTO's PatentsView API and caches it in a local SQL database (SQLite) plus in-memory graph for fast repeat queries. No data pre-committed — pulls per-query.
candidates.why_useful: Same patent-monitoring gap (#15) as above but with a caching/graph layer that would let a team build a citation-network view of Airbnb's (or a competitor's) patent portfolio without repeated API hits.
candidates.size_hint: tool only, DB built on first run

candidates.name: spinov001-art/patent-api-toolkit
candidates.what_it_holds: Python toolkit (no stars yet, very new) advertised as searching 8M+ US patents via the free, keyless USPTO PatentsView API for patent research/competitive intelligence.
candidates.why_useful: Another keyless PatentsView wrapper for gap #15; low-maturity repo so treat as a fallback option, not primary.

candidates.name: Ethan3600/USPTO-Trademark-API
candidates.what_it_holds: Small client (GPL-3.0, 6 stars, updated Feb 2026) that pulls trademark status data from USPTO's TSDR (Trademark Status & Document Retrieval) system — i.e., a scriptable way to check a company's live trademark filings/status by serial or registration number.
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-theme for the trademark half of gap #15 — could be pointed at Airbnb's trademark filings (new brand names/features, e.g. product or program launches often get trademarked ahead of announcement) as an early product-signal proxy.
candidates.time_coverage: current TSDR records, no historical archive

candidates.name: CanadianBaconBoi/WaybackMachineDiff
candidates.what_it_holds: Small diff viewer (1 star, updated Dec 2024, no license set) for comparing two Wayback Machine snapshots of a page, with automatic HTML-to-Markdown conversion to make diffs readable.
candidates.why_useful: Generic Wayback-diff tool matching gap #17's 'Wayback Machine tooling (archived airbnb.com pages...)' request — could be pointed at archived Airbnb help-center or press pages to detect changes (fee-policy wording, new-feature announcements) over time, complementing the fee-panel search-page capture already running per CLAUDE.md.

notes: This theme returned very thin results on GitHub. Zero hits for 'crt.sh certificate transparency python' (crt.sh tooling exists mostly as generic recon/OSINT scripts embedded in larger bug-bounty toolkits, not standalone repos matching the query, and those that exist are security-recon focused with no finance/product-launch framing — none worth flagging). Zero hits for 'app store release notes scraper', 'help center change monitor scraper', and 'certificate transparency subdomain monitor' as repo-search phrases — app-store-changelog and help-center-diff tooling appears to live inside larger app-store-scraper packages (e.g. facundoolano/app-store-scraper, itunes-app-scraper) rather than as dedicated release-notes-history repos; those broader app-store-scraper packages were not independently verified in this pass and could be worth a follow-up gh search on 'app store scraper' / 'itunes scraper' / 'google play scraper' by another agent, since they would let a team pull Airbnb's own App Store/Play Store version history and review counts as an engagement proxy (gap #5). PatentsView/USPTO clients were the only reliably on-theme, working results; none of them ship Airbnb-specific data, they are acquisition methods only, consistent with a 'product-launch monitor' theme being mostly a methods/tooling gap rather than a stored-dataset gap. WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted (200/200) before I could cross-check with web search, so this pass relied solely on gh CLI; a re-run with search budget available, or targeted gh searches for 'app store scraper', 'play store scraper changelog', and 'crt.sh osint' specifically, would likely surface more.
